intro_html: Ground turkey simmered with coconut milk, ginger, turmeric, and fish sauce while the rice cooks right in the same skillet, soaking up every drop of curry. One pan, zero drained pots, and each bowl delivers 31 grams of protein for about $3.55 (at everyday cost). Takeout flavor without the takeout invoice.
cost_closing_html: About $3.55 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a coconut curry that Thai takeout would charge $14 for before the delivery fees pile on. Fourteen bowls here costs roughly what two delivered ones do.
shop_smart: Coconut milk is the number two cost at about $1.85 a can. Store brands run under $1.50 and work fine in a simmered curry, so compare before you grab Thai Kitchen.
Fish sauce and soy sauce look like an investment on trip one, but both last a year in the pantry. This batch only used about $1.87 of the two combined.
Zucchini and carrots are the flex vegetables here. If squash or whatever is cheaper that week on the board, swap it in. The curry does not check IDs.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground turkey in your biggest deep skillet or pot over medium-high, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reads 165 F.
Add the grated ginger, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon and stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the sliced carrots, then add the dry rice and stir to coat it in the spices.
Pour in the coconut milk, chicken broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low about 15 minutes.
Scatter the chopped zucchini on top, cover again, and cook 5 to 8 more minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest 5 minutes off heat, then fold in the fresh basil and taste for salt and pepper.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each of 14 containers and every bowl comes in at 640 calories and 31 grams of protein.
